description: Comprehensive mobile app and authentication security hardening initiative based on deep audits of the iOS/Android apps, auth flow, and security posture. Covers server-side password policy enforcement, CSRF protection on auth endpoints, concurrent session management, enhanced mobile auth UX, MFA enforcement during login, session invalidation on credential changes, account lockout recovery, device trust and anomaly detection, step-up authentication, and mobile-specific security improvements. Priority 1 items are critical security gaps. Priority 2 are high-impact UX/security. Priority 3 are polish and completeness.

userStories.title: Add server-side password policy enforcement to edge functions
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want server-side password policy enforcement in the verify-auth-otp and reset-password-otp edge functions so that weak passwords cannot bypass client-side validation. Currently the verify-auth-otp schema only enforces min 8 chars (z.string().min(8)) and reset-password-otp does the same. Neither checks for uppercase, lowercase, numeric, or special character requirements. Add a shared validatePasswordStrength() function in supabase/functions/_shared/password-policy.ts that enforces: min 8 chars, at least 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 special character, and rejects the top 100 most common passwords. Apply this validation in verify-auth-otp (for invite_user and reset_password types) and reset-password-otp (verify action) before password is set.

Password policy requires: min 8 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 special character

reset-password-otp/index.ts calls validatePasswordStrength before updating password in verify action
Invalid passwords return 400 with specific validation error messages

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Created supabase/functions/_shared/password-policy.ts with validatePasswordStrength(). Applied to verify-auth-otp/index.ts (invite_user and reset_password types) and reset-password-otp/index.ts (verify action). Enforces min 8 chars, uppercase, lowercase, digit, special char, and rejects top 100 common passwords.

userStories.title: Add CSRF token validation to auth forms (SignIn, SignUp, ForgotPassword)
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want CSRF tokens validated on all auth form submissions so that cross-site request forgery attacks cannot hijack authentication flows. The CSRF infrastructure exists (csrfProtection.ts generates/stores tokens, csrfProtection.tsx provides useCsrfToken hook and CsrfTokenField component) but is NOT used in any auth forms. Wire up CSRF protection: (1) In SignInForm.tsx, add CsrfTokenField to the form, (2) In SignUpForm.tsx, add CsrfTokenField to the signup form, (3) In the parent Auth.tsx page, validate the CSRF token before calling signIn/signUp by reading the token from the form data and comparing with getCsrfToken() using validateCsrfToken(), (4) Add a useCsrfToken() call in the Auth page component to ensure a token is generated on mount, (5) Show an error toast if CSRF validation fails.

userStories.title: Add concurrent session management with configurable limits
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want concurrent session limits so that credential sharing is detectable and controllable. Currently users can have unlimited concurrent sessions with no visibility or control. Create a session management service: (1) Create src/lib/security/sessionManagement.ts with functions: registerSession(userId, deviceInfo), checkSessionLimit(userId, maxSessions=3), getActiveSessions(userId), terminateSession(sessionId), terminateAllOtherSessions(userId, currentSessionId). (2) The functions should use the existing user_sessions table in Supabase. (3) On login success in AuthContext.tsx, call registerSession with device info (user agent, screen size). (4) If session limit is exceeded, prompt user to terminate oldest session or cancel login. (5) Add a useActiveSessions hook that returns active session list for settings pages.

userStories.title: Add MFA verification step during login flow
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want MFA-enrolled users to be prompted for TOTP code during login so that stolen passwords alone cannot compromise accounts. Currently MFA setup exists but is never checked during the login flow. After successful password auth in AuthContext signIn(), check if the user has MFA devices enabled via Supabase MFA API. If they do, return a { mfaRequired: true } response instead of completing login. Create an MFA challenge step in the auth flow that prompts for TOTP code and verifies it before establishing the full session.

userStories.title: Add account lockout recovery via email
userStories.description: As a locked-out user, I want to unlock my account via email verification so I don't have to wait for the lockout timer. Currently users locked after 5 failed attempts must wait up to 60 minutes with no self-service option. Add: (1) An 'Account Locked - Unlock via Email' button on the lockout message in the sign-in form, (2) When clicked, send an OTP via send-auth-otp with type 'reauthentication', (3) On successful OTP verification, clear the failed login attempts via an edge function call, (4) The unlock flow should rate-limit to 3 unlock attempts per hour per email.

userStories.title: Add rate limiting to OTP verification endpoints
userStories.description: As a security engineer, I want per-email rate limiting on OTP verification attempts so that attackers cannot brute-force 6-digit codes. Currently verify-auth-otp has IP-based rate limiting but no per-email rate limiting on verification attempts. Similarly reset-password-otp verify action lacks per-email rate limiting. Add: (1) In verify-auth-otp, after parsing the request, check rate limit of 5 verification attempts per 15 minutes per email using checkRateLimit, (2) In reset-password-otp handleVerifyReset, add the same per-email rate limit check, (3) Return 429 with Retry-After header when exceeded.
